kept.q: Which of the following best defines the heat capacity of a body?
options: the quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of the whole body by 1 K
the quantity of heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K
the quantity of heat needed to melt 1 kg of a substance without changing its temperature
the quantity of heat lost per second by a hot body
kept.explanation: Heat capacity is the total quantity of heat needed to raise the temperature of a particular body (not per kg) by 1 K. It depends on the mass and specific heat capacity of the whole body.
kept.pidgin: Heat capacity na di total heat wey dem need to raise di temperature of di whole body (not per kg) by 1 K. E depend on di mass and specific heat capacity of di body.

kept.q: A block of metal has a mass of 2 kg and specific heat capacity of 400 J/kgK. Calculate the heat capacity of the block.
kept.explanation: Heat capacity C = mass x specific heat capacity = 2 kg x 400 J/kgK = 800 J/K.
kept.pidgin: Heat capacity C = mass x specific heat capacity = 2 kg x 400 J/kgK = 800 J/K.

kept.q: A kettle contains 3 kg of water at 25°C. Calculate the quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of the water to 85°C. [Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kgK]
kept.explanation: Heat required Q = mcΔθ = 3 x 4200 x (85-25) = 3 x 4200 x 60 = 756000 J.
kept.pidgin: Heat wey dem need Q = mcΔθ = 3 x 4200 x (85-25) = 3 x 4200 x 60 = 756000 J.

kept.q: Calculate the quantity of heat required to melt 0.5 kg of ice completely at its melting point. [Specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 334,000 J/kg]
kept.explanation: Heat needed Q = mL = 0.5 x 334000 = 167000 J. This heat changes the state of the ice without changing its temperature.
kept.pidgin: Heat wey dem need Q = mL = 0.5 x 334000 = 167000 J. Dis heat dey change di state of di ice but e no dey change di temperature.

kept.q: A 2 kg block of ice at -5°C is to be completely converted to water at 15°C. Using specific heat capacity of ice = 2100 J/kgK, specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 334,000 J/kg, and specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kgK, calculate the total quantity of heat required.
kept.explanation: Three stages: (1) warm ice from -5°C to 0°C: 2x2100x5 = 21000 J. (2) melt ice at 0°C: 2x334000 = 668000 J. (3) warm water from 0°C to 15°C: 2x4200x15 = 126000 J. Total = 21000+668000+126000 = 815000 J.
kept.pidgin: E get three stages: (1) warm di ice from -5°C to 0°C: 2x2100x5 = 21000 J. (2) melt di ice for 0°C: 2x334000 = 668000 J. (3) warm di water from 0°C to 15°C: 2x4200x15 = 126000 J. If you add dem, total na 815000 J.

kept.q: A metal block of heat capacity 200 J/K at 80°C is dropped into a liquid of heat capacity 800 J/K at 20°C inside a well-lagged container. Assuming no heat is lost to the surroundings, calculate the final common temperature of the mixture.
kept.explanation: Heat lost by metal = heat gained by liquid: 200(80-T) = 800(T-20). Expanding gives 16000-200T = 800T-16000, so 32000 = 1000T, giving T = 32°C.
kept.pidgin: Heat wey metal lose = heat wey liquid gain: 200(80-T) = 800(T-20). If you expand am: 16000-200T = 800T-16000, so 32000=1000T, T=32°C.
